==English== [[File:Chick.jpg|thumb|right|A baby chicken (chick), ''Gallus gallus domesticus'']] ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|chicke}}, {{m|enm|chike}}, variation of {{m|enm|chiken|t=chicken", also "chick}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ċicen}}, {{m|ang|ċycen|t=chicken}}. Sense of "young woman" dates to at least 1860 (compare {{m|en|chit|t=young, pert woman}}). More at {{l|en|chicken}}. ====Pronunciation==== * {{IPA|en|/t͡ʃɪk/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-chick.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪk|s=1}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun|s|chicken}} # {{senseid|en|Q1642639}} A [[young]] [[bird]]. #: {{hyper|en|bird|<|animal|<|creature#Noun|critter#Noun}} #: {{cot|en|birdlet}} #: {{nearsyn|en|nestling|fledgling}} ## {{senseid|en|Q65167027}} {{lb|en|especially}} A young [[chicken#English:_Q780|chicken]]. ##: {{hyper|en|chicken|<|poultry|<|bird|<|animal|<|creature#Noun|critter#Noun}} ##: {{cot|en|pullet|hen|cock|cockerel|rooster}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1961|author={{w|Norma Lorre Goodrich}}|title=The Medieval Myths|publisher=The New American Library|chapter=Beowulf|location=New York|page=41|passage=Neither '''chick''' nor child was left living the length of the seacoast.}} # {{senseid|en|Q3031}} {{lb|en|colloquial}} An attractive, young [[woman]]; or, more generally, a woman. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:girl|Thesaurus:woman}} #: {{ux|en|This '''chick's''' a machine but her friend is way more fun.}} #: {{ux|en|They're going to have a '''chick''' weekend. No guys allowed.}} #: {{ux|en|He'll fall for any '''chick''' with a nice smile.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1860|title=Tinsel and Gold: A Fireside Story|author=Joseph Verey|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=G0pWAAAAcAAJ&pg=PA155&q=%22pretty%20chick%22 |page=155|location=London|publisher=James Blackwood |passage="I thought you had some common sense, Frank," said Uncle John; "but I see you are as great a fool as all the rest. Marry, indeed! A pretty '''chick''' to marry!"}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1927|title=Elmer Gantry|author=Sinclair Lewis |passage=He had determined that marriage now would cramp his advancement in the church and that, anyway, he didn't want to marry this brainless little fluffy '''chick''', who would be of no help in impressing rich parishioners.}} #* {{quote-song|en|lyricist={{w|Artie Singer}}, {{w|John Medora}} and {{w|David White (musician)|David White}}|title={{w|At the Top|At The Hop}}|artist={{w|Danny & the Juniors}}||year=1957|text=Where the jockey is the smoothest
And the music is the coolest, at the hop.
All the cats and the '''chicks''' can get their kicks, at the hop.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|title=Bad moon rising|author=Tess Pendergrass |passage=I can't believe you've got a hot '''chick''' in that ratty apartment with you.}} # {{lb|en|military|slang}} A [[friendly]] [[fighter aircraft]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=Joe Welzen|title=The Gutsy Stomach Walker|page=50 |passage=The Aldis lamp flashes at the underside of each aircraft. It shows that the gear is down. Diegal is relaxing. This is such low responsibility, easy night duty. All the “'''chicks'''” (fighter aircraft) are home to roost except one.}} # {{lb|en|dated|endearing}} A young [[child]]. =====Derived terms=====
